question_text: Use the observer design pattern. Construct two Python classes. (a) WeatherStation has a private-by-convention list _observers and an attribute temperature, initially None. It has methods subscribe(observer), which adds the observer unless it is already subscribed; unsubscribe(observer), which removes it if present and does nothing otherwise; and set_temperature(value), which stores the value and then calls update(value) on every subscribed observer in the order they subscribed. (b) Display has an attribute readings, initially an empty list, and a method update(value) that appends value to readings. You do not need to write any other code.
adaptation_rationale: Original question written by Claude (single-agent Chunk 3 continuation, 2026-11-04) for a syllabus statement with no linked question at handover; no historical source question or official marking status claimed.

marking_points.criterion: WeatherStation constructor initialises _observers to an empty list and temperature to None.
subscribe adds an observer only if it is not already subscribed.
unsubscribe removes a subscribed observer and safely ignores one that is not subscribed.
set_temperature calls update(value) on every subscribed observer, in subscription order.
Display constructor initialises readings to an empty list.
Display.update appends the value to readings.

acceptable_alternatives: Accept try/except ValueError for safe removal. Accept iterating over a copy of the list. Minor syntax slips do not lose a mark if intent is unambiguous.
partial_credit_notes: Award each independent point once, up to 7 marks. Accept equivalent correct wording or valid alternative code. Do not double-credit one idea.

verification.scope: Singleton construction not assessed; Python has no enforced private access, so "private by convention" is stated.
